title: Uniform law on disjointness-coordinate vectors
statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, and consider the finite set of vectors $x \colon \{1,\dots,n\} \to \{\text{neither}, \text{left only}, \text{right only}\}$ assigning to each coordinate one of three labels, of which there are $3^n$ in total. Under the uniform probability law on this set, every subset $S$ of such vectors has measure
\[
\frac{\abs{S}}{3^{n}},
\]
where $\abs{S}$ denotes the number of vectors lying in $S$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
S is an arbitrary subset of the vectors indexed by Fin n valued in the three-element type DisjointCoordinate
the measure is the uniform law on the full space of such vectors
replaced: The uniform law on disjoint-coordinate vectors assigns mass by normalized cardinality.
